items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Well, I went with Ridgely. See, Ridgely made up a band. See, I went with Ridgely, paid with Ridgely down at Pete Hoyman's place.

ctx.x: Any of the other guys in the band play drums?

Yeah, Raymond Brown. He would play. Then Handley, he would get on the drum, you know. Play a waltz, you know, until I come back. Yeah. Then after I left there in 29, around 20, yeah, I don't know, around 27, I played there about a year, 28. Celestine and Ridgely's band broke up then. That's when the band split. Well, I went with Ridgely. See, Ridgely made up a band. See, I went with Ridgely, paid with Ridgely down at Pete Hoyman's place. What do you call it? Planetation? Yeah. Planetation. That's right. I worked…
Shots, Handy, Sales. What did Handy play in those days? Alto and clarinet. Did he play much clarinet then? Oh, lots of clarinet. I can't think of this one. I'm a mic now.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Yeah, we played spot jobs with Pierron's band, played spot jobs with Ridley's band.

ctx.x: Was this, didn't you play many spot jobs around during the time you were with Sam? Oh yeah. How do you play, I mean with other bands I'm talking about?

Yeah, we played spot jobs with Pierron's band, played spot jobs with Ridley's band. Yeah, all the bands. You see, played all these colored dance halls with Pierron, played all white. With Ridley, played white. Country club, Southern Yacht club.
No, no, what I mean is if you're working regular with Sam, and he's not working that night, would you take a job with another band? Oh yeah, yeah, if they need me, yeah.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Now when I was playing with Ridley, when David Jones would take a solo

ctx.x: What? Yeah, that's right. Did they ever have bands like that when you remember? I might have been. I don't know. I just wondered if they had any guys that played clarinet and trombone together, you know, would really be featured like that.

Be featured like? Like solos, trombone and clarinet? Well a duet really, the two of the together. Oh no, hardly. Hardly, huh? Hardly. Because you know they didn't know that much about music to play on. Cards you know. They just played on. Well I don't mean cards. I mean tailgate. Yeah. But I know like Yank and them used to play. But most of the time when Buddy would take a solo in our band, they would take down, you see. Now when I was playing with Ridley, when David Jones would take a solo, the bands would take…
